historia.title: History, Architecture and Art

iberico_content.title: The Heroic Sanctuary of El Pajarillo (4th c. BC)
iberico_content.body:
Strategically overlooking the Jandulilla river valley, the Iberian Sanctuary of El Pajarillo is one of the most remarkable archaeological discoveries in the Iberian Peninsula. Dating to the mid-4th century BC, this monumental sanctuary was conceived as a stepped ceremonial terrace for the heroic apotheosis of an Iberian prince or chieftain.

At its summit stood the celebrated sculptural monument portraying a mythical combat between a young aristocratic warrior and an imposing wild beast: the fierce Iberian Wolf Head, flanked by guardian lions and winged sphinxes, embodying power, valor, and sacred memory.

iglesia_content.title: Church of the Immaculate Conception and Convent
iglesia_content.body:
Standing close to the sanctuary's landscape, the Church of the Immaculate Conception was built between the 16th and 18th centuries. The church exhibits a Latin cross layout with side chapels, carved ashlar masonry arches, and an elegant cupola over pendentives above the transept.

The adjoining conventual remains preserve traces of the Tuscan cloister, documenting centuries of monastic devotion that shaped regional society and creating an inspiring visual dialogue with the ancient archaeological substratum.

arte_content.title: Sculptural Treasures & Artistic Heritage
arte_content.body:
Carved from local white limestone by Iberian master sculptors, the artwork of El Pajarillo reveals classical Mediterranean aesthetics harmonized with native religious values. The dramatic intensity of the Wolf's Head — with bared teeth, alert ears, and snarling muzzle — is a recognized masterpiece of ancient European art.

Inside the church, the gilded Baroque altarpiece, sacred imagery, and historical devotional canvases complete a unified cultural ensemble accessible today through interactive digital media.

timeline.title: Chronological Milestones of the Site
timeline.subtitle: A journey across more than two millennia of history, from the 4th-century BC Oretan heroic sanctuary to the present day.

events.text: Construction of the heroic Iberian Sanctuary monument at El Pajarillo in honor of the Oretan hero.
Roman Republican presence and ritual transformation of the Jandulilla river valley.
Initial construction of the Church of the Immaculate Conception and monastic buildings.
Erection of the central cupola, Baroque gilded altarpiece, and Tuscan cloister.
Systematic excavations led by the University Institute of Iberian Archaeology.
Opening of the modernized, multilingual and fully accessible digital Interpretation Centre.
